content_voiceover: This forest plot looks at how East Asian genetic ancestry associates with the odds of having particular molecular subtypes of ALL, and it's a nice illustration of ancestry-driven biology. On the left, in red, are subtypes that are significantly less common with East Asian ancestry, B C R colon colon A B L one like ALL has an odds ratio of zero point three eight, C R L F two rearranged is zero point four one, and T cell ALL is also zero point four one, all with odds ratios below one, meaning East Asian ancestry is protective against these higher-risk subtypes. On the right, in blue, are subtypes significantly enriched in East Asian ancestry, P A X five alt has an odds ratio of one point seven seven, T C F three colon colon P B X one is one point nine eight, D U X four is two point eight four, and Z N F three eight four is three point nine one, all significant with p-values under point zero five. So East Asian patients are more likely to have these particular favorable-to-intermediate rearrangements, and less likely to have B C R colon colon A B L one like or T cell disease. This kind of ancestry data helps explain some of the population differences seen in ALL outcomes and subtype distribution.
keypoints: East Asian ancestry: lower odds of BCR::ABL1-like, CRLF2, and T-ALL
East Asian ancestry: higher odds of PAX5alt, TCF3::PBX1, DUX4, and ZNF384
Odds ratios range from 0.38 for BCR::ABL1-like to 3.91 for ZNF384
Ancestry helps explain population-level differences in ALL subtype distribution
keypoint_voiceover: East Asian genetic ancestry is associated with lower odds of B C R colon colon A B L one like, C R L F two, and T cell ALL, but higher odds of P A X five alt, T C F three colon colon P B X one, D U X four, and Z N F three eight four, with Z N F three eight four showing nearly a four-fold increased odds.
